note: THE OTHER OVERLAY, and the reason it is not `SearchablePopover` is announced rather than styled: this trigger says `aria-haspopup="menu"` over a `role="menu"` of `role="menuitem"` buttons, where the picker says `dialog` over a `role="listbox"` of `role="option"` rows. A menu MOVES DOM focus onto its items; a listbox keeps focus on one element and points with `aria-activedescendant`. Those are incompatible focus models, which is why the set holds two overlays and not one with a `role` prop. The panel PORTALS to the plinth's own resolved overlay host, so it is clipped exactly as the product clips it. `open` is `$bindable` and is deliberately left undriven — see its waiver.

note: THE PICK CANNOT BE CLOSED BY A WRITE-BACK, and the reason is a shape mismatch rather than a missing argument: `onSelect(itemId)` reports an ID STRING while `value` is a RECORD (`{id, name, img}`). Writing the id back would leave the trigger with a value it considers present and a name and image it cannot read, so it would render the placeholder art under a `has-value` class — a state no call site can produce. So the `value` knob is the honest way to see the filled trigger, and picking in the popover logs the id. Its popover PORTALS to the plinth's resolved overlay host and is a GRID of image tiles bounded 280–420px, which is one of the four capabilities issue 1458 measured and left when it declined to collapse this into `SearchablePopover`. MEASURED ON THIS PLINTH: the trigger computes `height: 28px` against its own `width: 140px; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1` (`fabricate.css:9156`), because Foundry's core `<button>` height is a SPECIFIED height and a specified height beats `aspect-ratio` -- and that block carries no Foundry button reset, unlike `InspectorActionButton` and `Chip`, which both carry one and record why. The 138px image inside is then clipped by the block's own `overflow: hidden`. Both shipped callers wrap the component in `.manager-essence-source-drop-zone`, which sets `height: 84px; aspect-ratio: auto`, so the squashed face has no call site and the primitive is not self-sufficient. That is a finding about the component rather than about this row, and it is exactly the kind the lab exists to surface.

note: `value` IS `$bindable` AND THE LAB PASSES IT ONE-WAY. Ten of the nineteen converted call sites write `bind:value`, and the harness cannot: it holds knob values in its own state and hands them down through a spread, so there is no binding for the component's internal `value = next` to reach. Nothing is broken by that — Svelte lets a `$bindable` prop be assigned locally when no binding exists, so the field still shows what is typed — and the `onInput(next, event)` write-back is what returns the string to the knob, so the loop closes through the CALLBACK half of the API rather than the binding half. That is the shape the nine callback sites already use. It is a MANAGER primitive with no scoped style at all: dropped under `.fabricate-app` it renders as an unstyled `<label>`, which is why this plinth wears the manager root.

note: ITS TOGGLE CANNOT BE CLOSED BY A WRITE-BACK, and this is the third shape of that failure on this page: `onToggle(id, nextSelected)` reports WHICH entry moved and WHERE IT WENT, and neither argument is the next `selectedIds` array. `writes` can only feed a callback argument straight into a knob, so there is nothing here for it to feed. The `selectedIds` knob is therefore how both faces are reached, and adding or removing a pill logs the pair and leaves the row where it was. Its ADD MENU is a real `SearchablePopover` since issue 1458, so this specimen also proves the pill row and the picker as two things rather than one hand-rolled widget.

note: SIX TONES ARE THE WHOLE RAMP, closed on purpose: a new state belongs on one of them, and a seventh would mean the state genuinely is not any of the six, which has not happened yet. An unrecognised tone FALLS BACK to `subtle` rather than rendering unstyled — four essence call sites once shipped `neutral` and `positive`, neither of which is in the ramp, and the result survived three review rounds because nothing anywhere fails on it. `data-status-pill` reports the RESOLVED tone, so the fallback is observable on the plinth.
